sheets.title: How a car works
sheets.purpose: A gasoline car turns fuel into motion. The engine makes torque, the drivetrain carries it to the wheels, and the driver controls both through pedals and steering.

parts.label: DRIVER
parts.what: The person issuing commands: how much power, which direction, when to stop.
parts.why: Every trace on this sheet starts with a human input.

parts.label: PEDALS AND STEERING
parts.what: Accelerator, brake and clutch pedals, and the steering wheel. In most modern cars the accelerator is a position sensor rather than a cable (drive-by-wire).

parts.label: ENGINE CONTROL UNIT
parts.what: A computer that reads the pedal and engine sensors and decides throttle opening, fuel quantity and spark timing for every cycle.
parts.why: The driver asks for power; the ECU decides how the engine produces it.

parts.label: FUEL TANK
parts.what: Stores gasoline. An in-tank pump sends it under pressure to the injectors.

parts.label: BATTERY
parts.what: Supplies the starter motor and electronics while the engine is off; the alternator recharges it once the engine runs.

parts.label: ENGINE
parts.what: Burns fuel with air in closed cylinders and turns the pressure into rotation of a crankshaft.

parts.label: TRANSMISSION
parts.what: Trades speed for torque. Low gears multiply torque to start moving; high gears let the engine turn slowly at cruising speed.
parts.why: An engine only produces useful power over a limited speed range; gears keep it there.

parts.label: DRIVEN WHEELS
parts.what: Receive torque through the differential, which lets the left and right wheels turn at different speeds in a corner.

parts.label: EXHAUST SYSTEM
parts.what: Carries burnt gas away. The catalytic converter reduces harmful emissions; the muffler reduces noise.

parts.label: WINDSHIELD
parts.what: Two layers of glass bonded to a plastic interlayer, so it cracks without shattering into the cabin.
parts.why: Bonded into the body, it also stiffens the roof structure and gives the passenger airbag something to push against.

parts.label: BODY STRUCTURE
parts.what: The welded steel shell that everything mounts to. Crumple zones at front and rear absorb crash energy; the cabin cell resists deformation.

parts.label: DOORS
parts.what: Hinged panels with steel intrusion beams inside, latched into the body so they stay closed in a crash.

steps.text: The driver presses the accelerator pedal.
The pedal moves; a sensor measures how far.
The position goes to the engine control unit as a signal, not a cable.
The ECU opens the throttle further and calculates how much more fuel to inject.
Injection and spark commands go to the engine every cycle.
More air and fuel per cycle means more pressure on the pistons: more torque. (Open the engine to see how.)
Torque leaves the engine through the flywheel.
In a low gear the transmission multiplies the torque.
The differential splits it between the driven wheels.
The tyres push against the road and the car accelerates.
Turning the key or pressing start connects the battery to the starter motor.
The starter spins the crankshaft so the cylinders begin to draw air.
The fuel pump delivers gasoline to the injectors.
The ECU times injection and spark from the crankshaft position.
Combustion takes over and the starter disengages.
Burnt gas leaves through the catalytic converter and muffler.

sheets.title: Inside the engine
sheets.purpose: A four-cylinder, four-stroke gasoline engine. Air and fuel burn in the cylinders, pistons push a crankshaft, and a camshaft driven at half crankshaft speed opens the valves in time.

parts.label: AIR INTAKE
parts.what: Filters incoming air and meters it with the throttle plate, which the ECU opens in proportion to the pedal.

parts.label: FUEL INJECTORS
parts.what: Electrically opened nozzles that spray a measured quantity of fuel each cycle; the ECU sets how long they stay open.

parts.label: CYLINDER BLOCK
parts.what: Four cylinders, each with a piston. They fire in a staggered order so that one of them is always on its power stroke.

parts.label: IGNITION
parts.what: Coils step battery voltage up to tens of thousands of volts and fire each spark plug at the moment the ECU chooses.

parts.label: CRANKSHAFT
parts.what: Offset throws turn the up-and-down motion of the pistons into rotation, like pedals on a bicycle.

parts.label: CAMSHAFT
parts.what: Lobes on a shaft push the intake and exhaust valves open at the right moment in each cylinder's cycle.
parts.why: A four-stroke cycle takes two crankshaft revolutions, so the camshaft is geared to turn at exactly half crankshaft speed.

parts.label: EXHAUST MANIFOLD
parts.what: Gathers exhaust from all four cylinders into one pipe leading to the catalytic converter.

parts.label: FLYWHEEL
parts.what: A heavy disc on the end of the crankshaft. Its inertia carries the engine between power strokes.

parts.label: TO TRANSMISSION
parts.what: Where engine torque leaves for the clutch or torque converter and the gearbox.

steps.text: Air enters through the filter and throttle.
Fuel is sprayed into the incoming air.
The spark plug ignites the compressed mixture. (Open the cylinder block for one cylinder's four strokes.)
Expanding gas drives the piston down and turns the crankshaft.
The flywheel smooths the separate power pulses into steady rotation.
Torque leaves for the transmission.
The crankshaft turns twice per four-stroke cycle.
A belt or chain drives the camshaft at exactly half that speed.
Each cam lobe opens its valve once per cycle, in step with the piston.
Opened exhaust valves release burnt gas into the manifold.

sheets.title: One cylinder, four strokes
sheets.purpose: Intake, compression, power, exhaust. The piston moves down, up, down, up; only the power stroke produces work, and the cycle takes two crankshaft revolutions.

parts.label: INTAKE VALVE
parts.what: Opens while the piston moves down so the cylinder fills with air and fuel.

parts.label: SPARK PLUG
parts.what: Produces the spark that ignites the mixture just before the piston reaches the top.

parts.label: EXHAUST VALVE
parts.what: Opens while the piston rises the second time so it can push the burnt gas out.

parts.label: COMBUSTION CHAMBER
parts.what: The space above the piston. Compression squeezes the mixture to about a tenth of its volume before ignition.

parts.label: PISTON
parts.what: A sliding plug that is pushed by the burning gas. Piston rings seal it against the cylinder wall.

parts.label: CONNECTING ROD
parts.what: Links the piston to an offset throw on the crankshaft, converting straight-line force into torque.

parts.label: CRANK THROW
parts.what: The offset journal on the crankshaft that the rod pushes around.

steps.text: **1 · INTAKE.** The piston moves down with the intake valve open; air and fuel are drawn in.
**2 · COMPRESSION.** Both valves close and the rising piston squeezes the mixture to about a tenth of its volume.
**3 · POWER.** The spark plug fires just before the piston reaches the top.
Burning gas expands and pushes the piston down hard.
The connecting rod carries that force…
…to the crank throw, turning the crankshaft. This is the only stroke that does work.
**4 · EXHAUST.** The exhaust valve opens and the rising piston pushes the burnt gas out. Two crankshaft revolutions per cycle.

blocks.p: A minimal example for the system-drawings skill: three sheets, from the whole car down to one cylinder.

blocks.note: Typical values are marked as typical; individual engines differ.
